name: Bijan Robinson

background.fact: Born January 30, 2002 in Tucson, Arizona. He attended Salpointe Catholic High School, set a state record with 7,036 rushing yards and 114 touchdowns, and as a senior was the Arizona Gatorade Football Player of the Year (2,235 yards and 38 touchdowns on 126 carries).

A five-star recruit, he went to Texas, was Alamo Bowl MVP in 2020 (10 rushes for 183 yards and a touchdown), ran for 1,127 yards in 2021 and 1,580 yards with 18 touchdowns in 2022, when he was a unanimous All-American and won the Doak Walker Award.

Atlanta drafted him eighth overall in 2023 (round 1, pick 8). He is listed at 5 ft 11 in and 215 lb, age 24, in his fourth NFL season, jersey 7. Combine: 4.46 forty, 37 inch vertical, 124 inch broad jump.

Career regular season through Week 9 of 2026: 60 games, 974 carries for 4,790 yards and 30 touchdowns, 229 catches for 1,988 yards and 10 receiving touchdowns, 6 lost fumbles, 15.1 fantasy points a game under league scoring. Best season by points per game: 2025 at 17.05 (1,478 rushing yards).
Contract details are empty in the data file. One search summary says he is under contract through the 2030 season; not confirmed by a second source.

family.fact: He is a Christian. His mother named him after the Iranian fashion designer Bijan, the Persian word for hero.
His great uncle is Paul Robinson, a former running back who played for the Cincinnati Bengals, Houston Oilers and Birmingham Americans.
Nothing about a spouse, partner or children was found in the sources reached: not found.

outlook_next_game.lean: plays a full workload; expected around 14 to 19 fantasy points
reasons: He is active with no listed injury and has had 77 to 82 percent of snaps in every game since Week 5, so volume is secure.
Atlanta is a 3 point home underdog with an implied total near 22, a script that is less run heavy than his away wins, and his home average is only 11.6 points.
Kansas City gives up about 84 percent of normal rushing yards to backs but more than normal receiving yards, so his catches may matter.
Risks: he scored a rushing touchdown in only 3 of 9 games (Weeks 3, 4 and 9), he can vanish as a receiver as at Tampa Bay, and a return of Brian Robinson could take carries.

scouts_read: Bijan Robinson is healthy and has been the centre of Atlanta's offence, with 72 percent of the team's carries and about 80 percent of snaps. Kansas City is a 3 point road favourite and allows fewer rushing yards than normal to running backs, though it gives up more receiving yards. That points toward a game with plenty of touches but modest efficiency, and his home games this year have averaged only 11.6 points compared with 22.7 on the road. If Brian Robinson returns, a few carries could move away from him. I would project a mid range game of roughly 14 to 19 points, with a touchdown deciding whether it goes higher.
